Port Cities. - Interests in port cities request that these cities be treated differently than other municipalities. The Greater Baton Rouge Port Commission proposes that the terminal areas of all port cities be the same size, regardless of the population of each city, for traffic having a prior or subsequent movement by water. It is suggested that this terminal area be defined by applying the maximum radius authorized for any city (20 miles) to every port city. It is argued that a uniform terminal area for all port cities will equalize competition between the ports of large and small cities. The Port Everglades Authority suggests the establishment of seaport commercial zones for traffic moving in foreign commerce having a prior or subsequent movement by water. It recommends that these zones be equal to three times the distance of any mileage formula established to determine the commercial zone of the seaport city.
These parties seem to be under the impression that the transportation of general freight having a prior or subsequent movement by water between points in a municipality's commercial zone, by a motor common carrier, where operations are otherwise subject to regulation under the Interstate Commerce Act, is exempt from regulation.
